Independent geometric checker built section-edge pairs and their Euclidean diameter for 175 sampled normals over n=2,3,4,5,8 with max difference 4.44e-16.
n=2 distribution integral exactly equals 1−4/pi atan(r) at six interior tested ratios; n=3 integral matches independently derived published spherical-angle formula at five tested ratios.

correctness.rationale: All generic section vertices are precisely crossed signed edges of the ℓ1 unit ball; central symmetry makes diameter twice the maximum Euclidean vertex norm. Pairwise norms are sqrt(a²+b²)/(a+b), maximized by the most unequal normal-coordinate moduli since f′(q)=(q−1)/((1+q)²sqrt(1+q²))≤0. Haar normal Gaussianization and conditioning on the maximum half-normal coordinate give the full finite-n CDF for n≥2. The minimum has n m_n⇒Exp(sqrt(2/pi)), the maximum satisfies M_n/sqrt(2log n)→1 in probability, giving n sqrt(log n)(2−D_n)⇒Exp(1/sqrt(pi)). For all fixed k, on M_n≥sqrt(log n) the scaled deficit is ≤2n m_n, whose moments are uniformly bounded by concavity of H near zero and Gaussian tails; the complement has superpolynomially small probability, so uniform integrability establishes k!pi^(k/2), mean and variance. n=2 is included; the CDF endpoints r=0,1 and support [sqrt(2),2] are correct. Finite independent brute-force checks cannot prove n→∞, which is analytically established.
residual_risks: Only generic normals are used in deterministic probability proof, justified by probability-one continuous Gaussian law.
The n→∞ convergence is nonuniform for varying codimension or changing body shape; only fixed codimension one and standard ℓ1 normalization are proved.

value.rationale: For the canonical ℓ1 cross-polytope, Euclidean diameter of a Haar central hyperplane section is a natural geometric-probability invariant closely tied by polarity to cube projection inradii. The theorem gives the entire finite-n law for the natural unbounded dimension family and an exact non-Gaussian endpoint scaling, rate and convergence of all fixed moments, information not determined by available concentration bounds or the n=3 spherical table. The min/max Gaussian coordinate reduction is a reusable structural mechanism; future researchers comparing random section inequalities can use its exact calibration of distributional tails. There is no claim of arbitrary codimension, arbitrary bodies, or a novel n=3 CDF.
residual_risks: Proof is elementary Gaussian extreme-value and polytope geometry, so significance rests on the complete natural distribution/limit rather than a general theory.

scientific_limitations: Proof assumes Haar central codimension-one sections of standard Euclidean ambient ℓ1 unit balls and does not imply arbitrary codimension.
Finite checks corroborate geometry/integrals but neither the limiting theorem nor moment uniform integrability.
Prior n=3 octahedron CDF is covered, not novel; broader historical priority remains best-of-knowledge.
